status: preliminary engineering concept - interface survey required
description: A load-bypass bridge pedestal that places the AM59-3S-64-64 immediately below the antenna rotator while preserving the existing BlueSky castle-cut pipe and plate. The amplifier is mounted horizontally on a removable cartridge. A low-restriction wet airflow bay is separated from a dry connector doghouse.

materials.outer_finish: light gray or white low-solar-absorptance powder coat
materials.hardware: corrosion-compatible locking hardware; final grade and isolation after structural review

interfaces.lower_existing_plate_pattern: UNRESOLVED - survey the user's current pipe/plate
interfaces.upper_rotator_pattern: UNRESOLVED - repeat the measured rotator base pattern and datums
interfaces.note: No production interface holes are intentionally modeled in v1. Do not match-drill or fabricate until plate thickness, bolt pattern, dowels, fastener grade, and load allowables are verified.

assumptions: The existing castle-cut pipe and its welded/bolted plate remain in service and are not redesigned.
The AM59 is installed with its OEM mounting lid down and airflow horizontal from fan end (-X) to output end (+X).
The four-post frame, not the amplifier or sheet-metal shell, carries all rotator and antenna loads.
The AM59-005D PDF supersedes generic AM59 web data for model-specific electrical and mass values.
The outer shell is splash/rain mitigation for portable deployment, not a certified NEMA or IP enclosure.
